cmrguard_20260819.bug: hero_crystal_maiden.lua's X.ConsiderR had zero self-preservation check before committing to Freezing Field's 10s self-rooting channel -- only counted enemies/escape math, never whether CM herself was about to be chain-CC'd. Systemic pattern across the 30-cast sample: 9/30 (30%) channels cut short (<2s of the 10s max), several immediately preceding a CM death. Cleanest frame: 20260819_003005_slot1 t=373.4 (6:13) -- CM opened R while Jakiro (ice_path off cooldown, curated hard-CC) was closing to ~1139 units with no ally CC covering him; he stunned her 0.6s into the channel and she died 5.9s later.
cmrguard_20260819.fix: new X.cm_IsRSafeToOpen(hBot) in hero_crystal_maiden.lua: withholds R (returns BOT_ACTION_DESIRE_NONE from ConsiderR) when a nearby enemy holds a ready hard-CC ability per the existing curated J.tHardCcAbilities table. [NARROWED 2026-08-19T11:53Z, GH #34] The first cut asked the boolean wrapper J.HasReadyHardCc and was RANGE-BLIND; it now takes the handle from J.GetReadyHardCc and requires GetUnitToUnitDistance(hBot,e) <= (hCc:GetCastRange() or 0) + X.nRGuardCloseBuffer, the same form ccburst's 2026-07-23 bisect settled on (no-target self-radius CCs report cast range 0 -> the holder must be on top of her). Buffer = 400, NOT ccburst's 250: that one sizes a 3s lane-trade window ('can he land it before I step away'), this one guards a 10s self-rooting channel a threat only has to reach ONCE; 400u is ~1.3s of hero movement at ~300 ms. Default path (candidate not armed) still returns true on the first line -- shipped behavior byte-identical. Also extended tests/mock/replay_fixture.lua to expose real per-slot ability handles via GetAbilityInSlot (general engine-plumbing fix, not gated).
cmrguard_20260819.validation: TWO real-frame fixtures pinned together (the director's explicit readmission condition, and the lanefix lesson that a locally-correct narrowing must not undo the original catch): (1) tests/fixtures/f_260819_003005_cm_selfpreserve.lua t=373.4, Jakiro ice_path ready at 1139u -- MUST BLOCK; (2) tests/fixtures/f_260819_004858_cm_centaur_far.lua t=423.4 (mined this session: AWS bootstrap + cached behav-dump on the real .dem + make_fixture.py), 31%-hp Centaur at 1326u whose hoof_stomp is a self-centered 325-radius AoE, walking monotonically away (1326->3077 over 10s) and never casting it; Ogre Magi is closer (346u) but his fireblast is 4s from ready, so the Centaur is the sole vetoer -- MUST PASS. Ground truth: CM opened Freezing Field on frame (2) for real and lived another 44.1s. Tests: tests/test_replay_260819_cm_r_range.lua (10 cases) + tests/test_replay_260819_cm_r_selfpreserve.lua (5, updated). Coverage includes gate OFF byte-identity, the release holding whether the engine reports hoof_stomp's cast range as 0 or as its 325 radius, two labeled mutations (Centaur walked to 350u vetoes again; the same enemy at his real 1326u given a 1000-range CC vetoes -- so the release is caused by DELIVERY RANGE, not by the ability falling out of the curated table), an assertion that the buffer stays inside the [139, 1001) window the two real frames bound, and two wiring assertions. FOUR mutation tests on the fix all caught: restore the boolean wrapper / buffer 1100 / buffer 100 / unwire the guard from ConsiderR. luacheck 0 warnings; full suite green (428/428 at commit time on the hero branch). [END-TO-END ADDED 2026-08-19T13:44Z] The validation above stopped at SOURCE-LEVEL wiring assertions because sAbilityList[6] was nil in every fixture, so X.ConsiderR short-circuited at abilityR:IsFullyCastable() before reaching the guard (GH #36, filed by this group, fixed by the director at 13:08Z via tests/mock/ability_meta.lua). With ultimates now reachable, the SAME two real frames drive the real X.ConsiderR() and the guard's effect on CM's FINAL bid is pinned for the first time (the director's rule 0b): on the 1326u Centaur frame armed bids BOT_ACTION_DESIRE_HIGH and EQUALS the shipped bid (the false positive no longer eats the ultimate); giving that same Centaur a 1000-range CC drops the bid to NONE (so the guard really is on the decision path, not decorative); on the 1139u Jakiro frame armed bids NONE while shipped bids HIGH (the gate is what withholds the channel that got her stunned 0.6s in and killed her). HONEST BOUNDARY of the end-to-end cases: ConsiderR's opening branch needs THREE enemies inside the field and only one stands that close on either real frame, so two enemies alive on the frame are walked in to 500u as a labeled MUTATION; the tests ASSERT those two hold no ready hard CC (J.GetReadyHardCc == nil), so the mutation moves the branch precondition and nothing the guard reads. Freezing Field's 835 AoE radius is an external anchor (Liquipedia); CM's distance from fountain is real (loader wires the map-constant fountains). 15 cases in tests/test_replay_260819_cm_r_range.lua; the two source-level wiring assertions are KEPT as cheap tripwires. Re-ran all four mutations: restoring the boolean wrapper and unwiring the guard are now caught by the END-TO-END cases, not only by the source assertions. luacheck 0 warnings; 449/449 green (baseline 444).
cmrguard_20260819.known_gap: (1) NOT fixed by the narrowing: GH #34 case #4 (skeleton_king hellfire_blast, ~550 cast range, vetoing from 620u while the threat only materialised 12.0s later and CM was ground 1.00 -> 0.03). l1xpsoak_DISPOSITION_20260819.reason: Condition (a) is structurally unprovable in the current design, not merely unproven. The single consumption point (mode_retreat_generic) discards the Vector that ShouldXpSoakLane returns -- the absolute anchor that was the whole point of the 20260819 redesign -- and only tests it for nil, then returns the same BOT_MODE_DESIRE_HIGH as lanesurv. Its entry condition is a strict subset of lanesurv's (1200/>=2 enemies vs 1100/>=1, same 3.0s window, same HP*0.75 threshold), so of 335 entry episodes across 12 games, 97.3% are judged identically by the already-promoted lanesurv; the 9 exclusive frames (2.7%) showed no attributable behavioral difference under frame-by-frame review. More games cannot fix this -- the bottleneck is mechanism indistinguishability, not sample size.
l1xpsoak_DISPOSITION_20260819.readmission_path: Strategy group makes the anchor actually drive behavior (Action_MoveToLocation + hold) so the mechanism is observably distinct from lanesurv, OR drops the separate id and folds the exit hysteresis into lanesurv's internal parameters. lanehyst_20260819.source: strategy work unit 2026-08-19, closing GH #28 (director ruling 06:55Z: l1xpsoak returned to the strategy group, readmission path = make the anchor drive movement OR fold the exit hysteresis into lanesurv)
lanehyst_20260819.decision: Took the SECOND path, with one refinement: the hysteresis lands GATED behind a NEW id 'lanehyst' rather than as an edit to the promoted default. Folding it straight into lanesurv would silently change shipped turbo behavior for every bot with no way to A/B it; a new gate keeps the shipped decision byte-identical and makes the change measurable on its own.
lanehyst_20260819.why_not_the_anchor_path: No safe seam. bots/mode_retreat_generic.lua defines only GetDesire() -- it has NO Think(), so the ENGINE's built-in retreat owns all movement (fountain routing, TP home, shrine, escape items). Holding a position from retreat means authoring a full Think replacement for the most safety-critical mode; and a mode-Think replacement is precisely the wiring the A1 mechanism analysis (l1xpsoak_MECHANISM_20260731) blamed for l1xpsoak's -50 gpm. The only other home, mode_laning_generic's Think replacement, is the condemned design that death-marched 144711 medusa.
lanehyst_20260819.change: J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst (jmz_func.lua): on a true frame it stamps bot.laneBurstLastFire = DotaTime(); when the base bar is missed and 'lanehyst' is armed, it keeps returning true for up to J.nLaneBurstHysteresisWindow = 2.0s past that stamp, provided no peel-capable ally arrived and incoming is still >= J.nLaneBurstHysteresisFloor = 0.40 of current HP. Every enemy leaving 1100 releases earlier still (existing early-out). Off the gate the stamp is written but never read -> shipped decision unchanged.
lanehyst_20260819.rationale_c: Schmitt trigger on a blinking binary control signal. GetEstimatedDamageToTarget is mana/cooldown-aware, so a nuke coming off cooldown / an enemy stepping 20u past 1100 / a mana tick flips the decision between adjacent frames; a retreat that wins the desire auction for one frame and loses it the next issues a move order and cancels it -- neither retreating nor laning. The codebase already applies the same medicine on the l1kite path (bot.laneKiteUntil kite-lock, added for watched 181046 CK flapping).
lanehyst_20260819.anti_parking_brake: TIME-BOUNDED on purpose, unlike the l1xpsoak hold (which released only on state change and could hold indefinitely). 2.0s can smooth a blink; it cannot become the force-passivity failure mode that rejected lf_recover / corefarm / l1xpsoak wave 1.

Non-empty check: forcing the gate closed makes exactly the 2 hold assertions FAIL. 381/381 tests, luacheck 0 warnings.

lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.source: director work unit 2026-08-19T09:xxZ; bug filed by replay-check as GH #31 (15 mirror games / 333 opportunity episodes, l1trade+l5combo both SILENT)
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.defect: bots/mode_team_roam_generic.lua: the L1-TRADE and L5-COMBO branches bid RemapValClamped(hp,0,0.5,NONE,0.92) -- 0.92 chosen explicitly to outbid the PROMOTED lanesurv retreat at BOT_MODE_DESIRE_HIGH=0.75. But GetDesire() pipes the helper's value through CapForLanePush, which soft-ceils any desire >0.9 to 0.72 whenever J.IsInLaningPhase() or J.IsPushing(). Both J.ShouldInitiateLaneKill and J.ShouldSupportComboKill HARD-REQUIRE J.IsInLaningPhase(), so the cap's trigger condition is a strict SUPERSET of the two branches' entire domain: the 0.92 literal was unreachable on every frame they could possibly fire, the effective bid (0.72) landed BELOW the 0.75 it was picked to beat, and the effective bid was NON-MONOTONIC in HP (healthy core 0.72, half-HP core ~0.90). Neither branch set bDefensiveCollapse, and the existing 'divecap' exemption is both collapse-only and itself unarmed.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.same_family_as: GH #29 (retreat guard chain priority inversion). Both are 'the desire the author wrote is not the desire the engine sees' -- an author-intended relative ordering silently destroyed by a downstream transform. Worth treating as a recurring class, not two incidents.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.fix: New frame flag bLaneKillCommit (mirrors the existing bDefensiveCollapse pattern), reset each frame in GetDesireHelper, raised inside the two lane-kill branches, and exempted in _divecap_CapForLanePush (4th param). No extra soak gate on the exemption: the flag is only reachable from inside branches already gated on 'l1trade'/'l5combo'. Cap behavior for every other path is byte-identical. The 0.92 literal was KEPT (not lowered to <=0.9): bidding just under a cap threshold is the same implicit coupling that produced this bug.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.shipped_default_impact: NONE. Both raise sites sit inside branches whose helpers return nil unless turbo AND the soak candidate is armed, so with all gates off the flag is never raised and CapForLanePush is unchanged. Pinned by a source-level containment test, not just by inspection.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.validation: tests/test_lanekill_bid_reachable.lua (6 tests): drives the REAL global GetDesire() end-to-end (not the trigger helpers) and asserts the engine receives 0.92 and that it exceeds 0.75, for both ids; asserts the effective bid is monotone non-decreasing over a 21-point HP sweep; asserts a non-exempt roam desire is still capped to 0.72; and asserts at the source level that 'bLaneKillCommit = true' occurs exactly twice, each structurally inside a gated trigger branch carrying the ShouldReleaseLaneCommit guard. MUTATION-CHECKED twice: deleting the exemption (byte-equivalent to the pre-fix source) fails 4 tests including both end-to-end ones reporting the 0.72 clobber; deleting one raise site fails exactly the 2 relevant tests. Full suite 396/396, luacheck 0 warnings.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.coverage_gap_it_closed: GH #31 sec.4 was right about the root cause of survival: tests/test_l1_trade.lua and tests/test_l5_combo.lua only ever asserted the TRIGGER (J.Should*), and tests/test_divecap_gate.lua only the cap predicate in isolation. Nothing asserted their COMPOSITION -- the number the engine actually receives. That composition is now covered. Any future branch in this file whose comment reasons about a relative desire ordering should get the same end-to-end assertion.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.why_no_real_frame_fixture: The two helpers' decisive gates (lethality: combined castable burst >= target HP + 4s regen; self-risk: their burst vs mine) both run GetEstimatedDamageToTarget, which the behav dumper does not record (GH #27, GH #28 both flag the same gap). So no archived frame can be replayed into a state where the trigger provably returns non-nil -- a fixture could pin the geometry but not the firing. The defect is also a domain-wide arithmetic fact (cap domain superset of branch domain), which a single frame cannot express: the monotonicity sweep is the honest form of that claim.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.READING_IMPACT_on_prior_batch_data: IMPORTANT for whoever reads the 14-id 4-seed -34.59 gpm residual: l1trade and l5combo were armed in that wave but were bidding 0.72, never the designed 0.92. Their contribution to that number is NOT a measurement of the rule as designed -- they were not inert (0.72 still competes) but they were not the rule either. tpdying_20260819.source: strategy work unit 2026-08-19T11:5xZ, backlog item 8 (the 'final bid reachability' sweep). First id audited from the group's untouched list: tpcommit. GH #35.
tpdying_20260819.defect: J.GetTpCommitDefendDesire pins a fresh TP responder in the answered lane's DEFEND mode with a 0.85 floor, and releases the pin on `J.GetHP(bot) < 0.40 or J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst(bot)`. The second clause is the ANTICIPATORY one -- the reason the release works at all, since a lander who waits for 40% has already eaten the burst -- but J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst hard-requires J.IsInLaningPhase() on its third line. The floor is only reachable from the two response-TP branches (J.GetRescueTpTarget / J.ShouldTpSupportTowerFight), which require level 6+ and a >3500u trip, so the frames it actually pins are overwhelmingly POST-laning. There the release degrades to the numeric clause alone: the pin holds until the lander is ALREADY losing. That is the same 'ground down in place' shape (wave12 dossier mechanism D, ~6/24 landing deaths) the release was written against, minus the half that made it work. Same family as GH #29 / #31 / #32: a condition whose DOMAIN does not cover its branch's domain.
tpdying_20260819.change: New pure predicate J.IsIncomingBurstLethal(bot, nWindow) -- the same mana/cd-aware estimator J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst runs over the enemies within 1100, without the laning gate; true when their castable burst already covers the bot's current health. Consumed by ONE new gated release clause inside J.GetTpCommitDefendDesire, immediately after the shipped release: `if J.IsSoakCandidate('tpdying') and J.IsIncomingBurstLethal(bot, 3.0) then release end`. Reachable only inside the existing 'tpcommit' gate, so both shipped play AND today's armed-tpcommit behavior are byte-identical until 'tpdying' is armed.
tpdying_20260819.rationale_c: Two grounds. (1) Internal: the shipped release's own comment states the contract -- '丢失了动手机会才会走', a lander who is dying has lost the chance. This restores that contract in the domain the floor runs in; nothing new is claimed. (2) Standard strategy: whether to hold a contested spot is decided on incoming damage vs effective HP, not on a fixed HP percentage -- a 100% HP support inside a lethal combo should leave, a 45% HP hero out of range should not. Anticipating burst rather than reacting to an HP threshold is the same principle the PROMOTED lanesurv rule already ships on.
tpdying_20260819.conservatism: The armed path can only RELEASE a pin (return nil sooner) -- it can never raise or create one, and it cannot fire at all unless 'tpcommit' is armed too. Structurally it cannot add commitment, the same separability argument that let capmono ship ahead of divecap. One lever: the floor VALUE (0.85), the 12s window and the shipped release are all untouched.
tpdying_20260819.validation: tests/test_tpcommit_release_domain.lua -- 9 cases on the real frame f_182552_warlock_ult_hoard (t=626.0 / 10:26; Warlock 546/1022 = 53.4% HP; sniper 1008u away; replay ground truth: sniper dealt 669 into that 546 pool, died_after = 2.3s). Every desire assertion drives the REAL mode files -- bots/mode_defend_tower_mid_generic.lua and bots/mode_retreat_generic.lua GetDesire() -- per the test_set.md 0b rule: armed tpcommit -> defend bids 0.85 vs retreat -0.05 on the frame the hero was being killed; shipped-only -> 0.1; +tpdying -> back to 0.1. Containment: tpdying alone (no tpcommit) changes nothing, a survivable 100-damage burst keeps the pin, non-turbo keeps the pin. Reverse assertion: the shipped release is still exactly the laning-only pair (39% releases, 41% does not), so the test self-reports as obsolete if anyone makes the shipped release domain-correct.
tpdying_20260819.mutation_tests: Two. Deleting the gated clause (= pre-fix source) fails exactly the one armed assertion, printing the real pin (got 0.85). Forcing the gate always-on fails exactly the 2 shipped-behavior assertions. 427/427 tests, luacheck bots game 0 warnings.
tpdying_20260819.tooling_note: Getting a FINAL-BID assertion out of the TP/defend family needed four mock-fidelity repairs, all reusable by the whole team: BOT_MODE_DESIRE_* / BOT_ACTION_DESIRE_* now carry their real 0..1 values instead of the auto-const metatable's arbitrary ids (before this, Defend.GetDefendDesire returned 1008/1009 and no cross-mode bid comparison was meaningful); mock Vector gained Normalized/Length/Length2D/Dot; handle-returning getters (GetAttackTarget/GetTarget/GetCurrentActionTarget) answer nil rather than 0, and NumModifiers answers 0; the fixture loader wires the REAL per-team unit:DistanceFromFountain() from the shipped fountain constants. Net effect: bots/mode_defend_tower_*_generic.lua and bots/mode_retreat_generic.lua can now be dofile'd and their GetDesire() driven on a real frame. All 418 pre-existing tests stayed green through the change.

roamstale_20260819.source: strategy work unit 2026-08-19T15:xxZ, backlog #8 (final-bid / final-ACTION reachability sweep). Audited id: 'ownhalf'. The bid audit came back CLEAN -- on ownhalf's own motivating frame the collapse bid survives CapForLanePush at 0.72 and WINS the mode auction (laning 0.446, every other mode 0). The defect is one level further down, in the ACTION.
roamstale_20260819.defect: bots/mode_team_roam_generic.lua: the file-local `hTargetCreep` has exactly ONE writer -- the last-hit branch of GetDesireHelper -- which sits BELOW all six early-returning desire branches (X.ConsiderHelpWhenCoreIsTargeted [SHIPPED], ConsiderHelpAlly [SHIPPED], J.ShouldPunishDive ['ownhalf'], J.ShouldPunishOverchase ['overchase', armed], J.ShouldInitiateLaneKill ['l1trade'], J.ShouldSupportComboKill ['l5combo']), and it is never reset. Think() reads it FIRST and `return`s on it, before every Action_AttackUnit(targetUnit) path. So on every frame one of those six branches wins the desire auction, this mode's Think attacks LAST FRAME'S creep and never touches the collapse/commit target the desire was computed from. Desire says 'collapse on the invader', action says 'keep last-hitting'.
roamstale_20260819.family: Director's test_set.md 0b, ACTION-class variant (the GH #37 shape, not the GH #31/#32/#35 bid shape). Eighth example overall; the first one where the bid is provably INTACT and winning and the mode's own Think discards it.
roamstale_20260819.change: Gated turbo + J.IsSoakCandidate('roamstale'): clear hTargetCreep at the top of GetDesireHelper, beside the existing bDefensiveCollapse / bLaneKillCommit resets. Armed, the variable means what its only writer and its only reader both assume: THIS frame's last-hit creep. Shipped defaults keep the stale handle byte-for-byte.
roamstale_20260819.separability: The last-hit branch reassigns hTargetCreep on every frame that reaches it, so the armed delta is confined to exactly the frames an early branch returned. Armed can only ever REMOVE a stale creep attack, never add one, and it changes NO desire value anywhere (nothing reads hTargetCreep before its assignment) -- same shape of argument as capmono's 'pure min'.
roamstale_20260819.rationale_c: (1) The variable's name, its only writer and its only reader all mean 'this frame's last-hit creep'; only the missing reset disagrees. (2) Standard strategy: a hero that has decided to collapse on an isolated invader does not spend the window last-hitting -- the whole value of punishing an over-extension is that it is time-boxed. (3) This mechanically explains the watched behaviour that motivated 'ownhalf' in the first place (232228: WK, 100% HP, stun off cooldown, hovering ~1000u from a 69% solo Juggernaut for 17s while the punish branch was bidding for him) without needing any assumption about what the punish bid was.
roamstale_20260819.known_effect_on_other_ids: Un-blocks the ACTION for 'ownhalf', 'overchase' (currently ARMED), 'l1trade', 'l5combo' and the two SHIPPED help-ally branches. That breadth is why it must be measured on its own and NOT armed in the same wave as a bisect of any of those ids.

Controls: no-creep control proves the creep IS the mechanism; ordinary-last-hit frame is identical armed vs unarmed; non-turbo unchanged; a reverse assertion on the writer count self-expires the file if someone fixes the asymmetry properly. roamstale_ADMISSION_AND_WAVE_RULING_2026.decision: Admit `roamstale` (GH #39) to the armed test set (15 -> 16 ids). Next wave = PATH C: a two-arm bisect whose ONLY varying variable is roamstale (arm A = all 16, arm B = 16 minus roamstale). This OVERRIDES batch-desk's 16:10Z path A / path B choice.
roamstale_ADMISSION_AND_WAVE_RULING_2026.why_not_path_B: batch-desk #40 proposed bisecting the 12-id residual in halves on the default assumption that some individual id carries the -32.19. Director read mode_team_roam_generic.lua directly and rejected that assumption: hTargetCreep (L47) has exactly one writer (L287, the last-hit branch) which sits below SIX early-returning desire branches (L203 ConsiderHelpWhenCoreIsTargeted, L213 ConsiderHelpAlly -- both SHIPPED, both sides -- plus L225 ownhalf, L239 overchase, L258 l1trade, L275 l5combo -- four armed on the CANDIDATE side only), it is never reset, and Think() reads it FIRST (L461) and returns on it. So the candidate side has 4 MORE early-return branches than the baseline side, and therefore a structurally higher rate of 'team_roam wins the auction, then discards its own action and walks at last frame's creep' -- for reasons unrelated to the merit of any of those 4 rules. It is not benign: the discarded frame REPLACES whatever the baseline side would have done. Any halving of the 12-id residual splits those 4 branches across both arms, so BOTH arms would measure the same artifact. Remove the confound first.

tpdead_20260819.source: strategy work unit 2026-08-19T17:xxZ, backlog #5 / GH #37 (lf_rescue landing reachability), taken up once the lf_rescue bisect verdict landed (GH #40) and the director's code freeze lifted. Director routed #37 to this stream and left the choice among its three candidate fixes to us, to be pinned on the acceptance triple.
tpdead_20260819.defect: A rescue TP that never arrives keeps its landing commitment anyway. J.GetRescueTpTarget stamps bot.tpRespondLoc/-Until at cast; J.GetTpCommitDefendDesire then floors the responder's DEFEND bid at 0.85 for the whole 12s window. The replay desk's 11 tracked rescues arrived inside the modelled ~4s window ONCE (median landing->ally 2289u, worst 5858u), so the ordinary case is: ally dies mid-trip, responder lands at a tower, and the floor keeps walking it at a fight that is over. Nothing in the commitment ever asks whether the rescue is still a rescue -- the stamp is a LOCATION, and a location cannot die.
tpdead_20260819.candidates_falsified: Both earlier candidates die on the same acceptance triple. Candidate 1 (ceiling on landing->ally distance): the frame that must be REJECTED lands closer (1579) than the frame that must be ALLOWED (1746) -- pinned 2026-08-19T13:45Z. Candidate 2 (feed the walk time back into J.WillAllySurviveTpWindow's window): now falsified too, with the per-event damage timeline the fixtures gained this round. At each frame's own arrival window the gate's own comparison (incoming hero damage vs current HP) reads A 548/430 veto (right), B 96/225 allow (wrong), C 258/246 VETO (wrong -- that is the one rescue in the wave that worked; Axe lived on regen + salve, which the gate does not model). The dumper undercounts damage, so 258 is a FLOOR: more data can only make the veto of C more certain. Widening the window therefore trades the whole value of lf_rescue away.
tpdead_20260819.change: Gated turbo + J.IsSoakCandidate('tpdead'), reachable only inside 'tpcommit'. (1) ability_item_usage_generic.lua: the rescue branch also stamps bot.tpRespondAlly = hRescueAlly; the two place-answering response TPs (mid tower fight, defend TP) clear it. Inert state -- nothing reads it off the candidate. (2) jmz_func.lua J.GetTpCommitDefendDesire: with tpdead armed, if tpRespondAlly is stamped and no longer alive, drop tpRespondUntil/tpRespondAlly and return nil. Floor value, commitment window and both existing releases are untouched. nVsMe < HP*0.70 NOT touched (director's pinned boundary).
tpdead_20260819.separability: Same one-directional shape as tpdying: the branch can only turn a floor into nil, never raise or create one -- asserted over both stamp shapes on all three frames. Single-arming tpdead is a bit-identical no-op (it sits below the tpcommit gate), so it must never be bisected alone. It cannot touch the two place-answering TPs, which clear the stamp.
tpdead_20260819.rationale_c: (1) The commitment's own contract is purpose-driven -- the owner's wording behind the survival release is 'you leave once you have lost the chance to act'. A rescue whose target is dead has lost it by definition. (2) Standard play: nobody holds position at a tower for the remainder of a rescue window after the rescued hero is already dead; you regroup or take the freed time elsewhere. (3) It is the only one of the three candidates decided by EXACT ground truth (DEATH events), not by a damage estimate the offline data cannot reproduce.

axebuyblink_20260819.source: hero-stream backlog #5, the half that was still open (a real frame with Axe holding a dagger). Went looking for that frame in four archived turbo games and found the reason it does not exist.
axebuyblink_20260819.observation: Frame-by-frame item scan of four turbo soak games (soak/spot_20260819_121044_1_main, games 20260819_121916 / _122445 / _123032 / _123546, slot1, behav-dump 0.5-1.0s): Axe NEVER held a Blink Dagger in any frame of any of the four. Final net worth 7834 / 8586 / 5556 / 4228; nobody else in those games held one either. His boots (last component of item_tank_outfit) completed at t=272 / 291 / 292 / 432 with net worth 2696 / 2672 / 2834 / 2650, and the games ended at 658 / 723 / 660 / 658s.
axebuyblink_20260819.bug: hero_axe.lua's pos_3 buy order is item_tank_outfit -> item_crimson_guard -> item_blade_mail -> item_blink, i.e. roughly 8.5k of purchases before blink's 2250 starts; pos_1 puts Blade Mail ahead of it. That is a normal-mode order running in a mode whose games end at minute 11, so the item that delivers Axe's entire kit (blink -> Berserker's Call -> Counter Helix procs -> Culling Blade reset) is never bought. Second-order consequence: the already-validated 'axeblink' guard (hold the dagger for Call) has no population to act on -- its consumption point requires a dagger Axe never owns.
axebuyblink_20260819.fix: BlinkFirstBuild(tList) in bots/BotLib/hero_axe.lua rebuilds the pos_1 and pos_3 lists FROM the shipped ones by moving item_blink to index 2 (straight after the starting-items bundle, which carries the boots) and leaving every other item in its relative order. Applied only when J.IsModeTurbo() and J.IsSoakCandidate('axebuyblink'); otherwise the shipped tables are untouched, so gate-off behaviour is byte-identical. Derived rather than duplicated so the shipped and candidate orders cannot drift apart.
axebuyblink_20260819.theory: Blink Dagger is the standard first big item on Axe in every mainstream build: it is not a chase or escape tool but the delivery system for Berserker's Call, and the rest of the kit is priced off the enemies the Call pins. Vanguard/Crimson Guard buy survivability but no initiation, so a melee initiator holding them can still only fight what walks into him. Turbo compresses the game to ~11 minutes, which makes a 3.6k defensive item bought before the 2.25k enabler a strictly worse ordering than in normal mode. Reachability is measured, not assumed: from Axe's own gold curves, blink bought straight after boots would have landed at 558.5 / 479.4 / 584.5s and never in the fourth game -- 3 of 4 games gain a blink with 100-240s of a decisive turbo game left, against 0 of 4 today.
axebuyblink_20260819.validation: tests/test_axe_blink_build.lua, 10 cases: gate-off pos_3 and pos_1 asserted byte-for-byte against transcribed copies of the shipped lists; armed-but-normal-mode unchanged (turbo-only); a DIFFERENT armed candidate ('wkbuild') unchanged; armed turbo puts blink at index 2 for pos_3 and pos_1 with a multiset-equality check (nothing added or dropped) and a subsequence check (every non-blink item keeps its relative order); the aliased positions pos_2/pos_4/pos_5 follow their base list armed and stay shipped unarmed; the reachability arithmetic evaluated against the list actually under test (it first asserts that ONLY the starting outfit precedes blink, so inserting anything there fails the test rather than silently invalidating the measurement); and a tripwire pinning the shipped pos_3 indices the measurement was taken against. FOUR mutation tests all caught: removing the gate (6 fails), dropping the turbo check (1), landing blink third instead of second (4), dropping blink instead of moving it (4). luacheck 0 warnings; full suite 499/499 green (baseline 489 + 10 new).
axebuyblink_20260819.known_gap: (1) Blink's 2250 gold is the one number not read from the replays (shop price anchor; same class as the GetManaCost anchors on wkreincarnmp/axeblink/zusult). Everything else -- per-frame net worth, per-frame item lists, boots timing, game length -- is off the .dem. (2) Net worth is not spendable gold at an instant, so the projected landing frames are approximations of the purchase moment. tparrive_20260819.defect: J.ShouldTpSupportTowerFight's winnability gate is structurally blind to the responder it is deciding for. The helper requires the responder be > 3500 from the threatened tower and picks its target from the enemies within 1200 of that tower; J.SafeToCommitFight scores only heroes within 1200 of that target. The responder is therefore at least 2300 units outside its own read (asserted on all three acceptance frames), so 'is this collapse winnable' is evaluated as though the TP never happens -- it actually asks 'is this fight already fine WITHOUT me'. The helper's own HEAT GATE makes the inversion systematic: the ally the count is sure to include is REQUIRED to be hurt or under hero fire. Net effect: the 1-ally-dived-by-2 collapse the fix exists for is refused (1 >= 2 false), while the 2v2 that needs nobody is allowed. Same family as GH #29/#31/#32/#34/#35/#37 (test_set.md 0b: the helper's reasoning quietly invalidated by the consumed mechanism), and it is the FIRST case where the invalidating mechanism is the CALLER'S OWN precondition rather than a downstream transform.
tparrive_20260819.change: Gated turbo + J.IsSoakCandidate('tparrive'), reachable only when midtp or suptp is armed (the helper returns nil otherwise). New PURE predicate J.SafeToCommitFightOnArrival(bot, target): J.SafeToCommitFight's two branches with the arriving responder counted -- its burst added to the lethal sum, its body added to the head count -- and the 'depthnum' +1 deep margin honoured unchanged. Call site becomes SafeToCommitFight OR (gate AND SafeToCommitFightOnArrival). J.SafeToCommitFight itself is NOT touched: it is a shared consumption path (0b ninth example) with many other callers.
tparrive_20260819.separability: Adding one ally can only raise both branches, so the armed read is a strict SUPERSET of the shipped one -- armed can ADD a response, never remove or REDIRECT one (asserted per frame, plus the predicate-level implication). Single-arming tparrive is a bit-identical no-op, same shape as tpdying/tpdead: it must never be bisected as an arm by itself. No interaction with roamstale (different mode file, different mechanism).
tparrive_20260819.intent_reversal: HONEST CONFLICT, stated up front: tests/test_mid_tp_support.lua pins the shipped rule verbatim -- 'a losing (outnumbered) tower fight must not pull a wasted TP', 1 defender vs 2 divers. That is exactly the rule this candidate disputes. It stays green only because the gate is off (forcing the gate always-on fails it, mutation 2). If tparrive is ever promoted, that test must be REWRITTEN, not deleted. The dispute is the arithmetic: 1v2 without the responder is 2v2 with it, at our own tower.
tparrive_20260819.rationale_c: (1) A defensive TP under one's own tower to even a dive is textbook Dota -- the defender also gets tower damage and its own creep wave, so parity-on-arrival understates rather than overstates the defenders' side. (2) The repo has already paid for the general lesson once, in the opposite direction: J.GetRescueTpTarget's exception was REWRITTEN off fixture f_071423_luna_chase because SafeToCommitFight's numbers branch counts a dying bot as a full fighter. Here the same branch omits a full-HP fighter that is definitely arriving. (3) The helper's own comment states the intent this restores: 'fires only when the collapse is winnable' -- winnable is a claim about the fight that will exist, not the one that exists now.

roamreach_20260819.mechanism: Chain proven at frame level. (1) 'ownhalf' -- and 'ownhalf' ALONE, isolated one id at a time -- opens J.ShouldPunishDive on the t=312.5 frame; team_roam bids the lane-capped 0.72 and WINS the auction (laning 0.446, every other mode 0). (2) Its Think issues Action_AttackUnit(target, false) -- the CONTINUOUS form: the engine pursues until the target dies or a new order arrives. (3) By t=318.5 not one branch of GetDesireHelper is true any more and team_roam bids 0, so another mode wins and the engine STOPS CALLING team_roam's Think -- which is where the only release this mode owns (the >1800 leash) lives. The order therefore keeps executing with neither justification nor any reachable release. One true frame of a collapse branch buys a cross-map chase.
roamreach_20260819.falsified: GH #45 section 3's conjecture ('the collapse branch keeps bidding while some retreat/leash force pulls back, so the bot is pinned in the ring') is WRONG in its first half: the branch stops bidding within 6 seconds and the chase continues anyway. No pull-back force is needed to explain the ring -- an unreleased attack-follow on a target with equal movespeed reproduces it exactly.
roamreach_20260819.roamstale_relation: This is the delivery half of roamstale, not a contradiction of it: shipped, the stale creep handle swallowed this very order (director's test_set.md J.4 (3): the stale handle's consequence is Action_AttackUnit on a dead handle doing NOTHING), which is why arm B shows no ring-idling while arm A does. roamstale made the order arrive; nothing bounds it once it has. NOT provable from these fixtures (a fresh fixture load has hTargetCreep nil), stated as inference from the arm A/B difference.
roamreach_20260819.change: Gated turbo + J.IsSoakCandidate('roamreach'), in bots/mode_team_roam_generic.lua only. Armed, a HERO target beyond that reach gets Action_MoveToLocation(its position) -- a FINITE order -- instead of the continuous attack-follow, at both hero-attack sites of Think (the help-ally site and the core/support site). In-reach targets and every non-hero target keep the shipped order byte-for-byte. No desire value changes anywhere.
roamreach_20260819.separability: Armed differs only on frames where team_roam's Think fires on a hero target outside the bot's own threat reach; the order still points at the same target, so the approach is unchanged while the mode keeps winning -- what changes is that the leftover order expires about one target-distance after the mode loses the auction instead of dragging the bot across the map. Armed ALONE is a bit-for-bit no-op (asserted): the gate is only reachable on a frame some collapse branch already won, so it CANNOT be a lone bisect arm -- same scheduling shape as tpdying/tpdead.
roamreach_20260819.rationale_c: Standard play: do not chase a hero you cannot catch without a way to close the gap (a lock, a slow, or an ally in front) -- the farm and map position you give up cost more than the kill you will not get. The engine-side half is mechanical: a continuous order is re-evaluated by nobody once its mode stops winning, so any commit it encodes must be bounded at the moment of issue.

fixture_last_seen_20260820.undeclared_world_assertion: tests/mock/bot_api.lua stubbed GetHeroLastSeenInfo(id) -> {} for every id, AND the fixture loader's GetTeamPlayers(team) ignored its argument and answered for OUR team whichever team was asked for. Every reader is shaped `for _, id in pairs(GetTeamPlayers(GetOpposingTeam())) do local info = GetHeroLastSeenInfo(id) ... info[1].location`, so the loop body was unreachable and J.GetLastSeenEnemiesNearLoc / J.GetLastSeenEnemies / every last-seen head count returned an EMPTY LIST on every fixture, on every frame. In plain words: 'nobody has ever seen an enemy anywhere.' Same family as GetTower, GetIncomingTrackingProjectiles, HasModifier (20260819) and WasRecentlyDamagedBy* (20260820T0145Z). The ALLY half of the GetTeamPlayers problem was fixed independently and in parallel by the director's GH #53 roster work (fixture_roles_GH53_20260820T0300Z); this entry adds the OPPOSING half and the memory itself, and the two were merged by hand at rebase.

Alive-only, matching the convention the unit lists already use (every shipped reader gates on IsHeroAlive, which the mock cannot answer per id). No fixture carries per-hero vision yet (GH #27) so every sighting is current; if `seen_by` ever appears, a hero the subject's team cannot see gets time_since_seen = 999 -- an unusable memory rather than an invented stale location.

GetTeam() hands out the engine's real 2/3, so every shipped `Team == TEAM_DIRE` comparison was silently false -- J.GetTeamFountain handed a DIRE subject the RADIANT fountain, i.e. every 'step back toward my fountain' location in a fixture pointed at the wrong corner of the map. defstale_20260820.gate: J.IsSoakCandidate('defstale') and J.IsModeTurbo(); shipped default unchanged
defstale_20260820.defect: aba_defend.DefendThink's bail-out -- the source's own comment calls it 'a small don't-walk-through-fire guard' -- reads `bot:WasRecentlyDamagedByAnyHero(5) and #pathEnemies > #ds.nInRangeEnemy`, i.e. 'more enemies on my PATH than IN RANGE'. Both sides are the SAME query, jmz.GetLastSeenEnemiesNearLoc(botLocation, 1600). `pathEnemies` is that query bucketed to 500ms on the bot handle; `ds.nInRangeEnemy` is that query written at the BOTTOM of GetDefendDesireHelper, below SEVEN early returns -- one of which (`#closeEnemiesDefend > 0 and #closeAlliesDefend >= #closeEnemiesDefend`) fires on exactly the frames DefendThink runs on, i.e. whenever a fight is happening within 900. bot._defend is never reset, so during a fight the right-hand side freezes at its pre-fight value, or at the initial empty table (0) if no call ever reached the bottom. The comparison is therefore bought entirely by staleness, never by a real path/range difference -- and when true the bot walks 700 back toward its fountain and returns, abandoning every other DefendThink branch for the frame.
defstale_20260820.family: Director's 0b family. Closest relative is roamstale (a state field written below early-returning bid branches and read first by Think), but the subtype is new: here the stale field is not a handle but a COUNT, and it is compared against a fresher copy of ITSELF, so the branch's stated meaning is unrepresentable rather than merely mis-targeted.
defstale_20260820.frames_pinned: tests/fixtures/f_260819_223607_drow_defend_bail.lua (20260819_223607_slot1, t=330.4): drow_ranger (Dire) 609/780 hp (78%), 929u from its own 56%-hp top T1, last hit by ogre_magi 3.8s earlier, exactly ONE enemy (necrolyte, 861u) inside 1600, helper returns 0.3 on all three lanes so nInRangeEnemy is still the empty table. GROUND TRUTH: it stayed -- last-hit a creep at t=332.6, 120 xp at t=336.9, 254 damage into ogre_magi between t=338.0 and t=339.9, and did not die for another 42.5s. CONTROL tests/fixtures/f_260819_222526_jakiro_defend_fresh.lua (20260819_222526_slot1, t=358.5): same lane and shape but outnumbered inside 900, so the helper skips the early return, reaches the bottom, writes a live count, and the guard is honestly false.
defstale_20260820.domain_measured: Over the 3 replays of the 22:25-22:36 wave, 1437 hero-frames have the shape 'under hero fire within 5s AND within 1600 of an own building AND >=1 enemy within 1600'. On a 45-frame sample of those, the guard's CONDITION is true on 32 (71%) -- 27 of them because nInRangeEnemy is still 0. Reachability is much narrower: a defend mode wins the SCRIPT auction on only 1 of those 45 (the pinned drow frame), because mode_retreat_generic usually outbids defend while a bot is under fire. On a separate 70-frame random sample, defend wins 26 times but never with the guard true. So this is a real, un-gated, wrong decision with a NARROW measured footprint -- and the footprint is a lower bound, since the engine's built-in modes have no script GetDesire (GH #27).
defstale_20260820.change: bots/FunLib/aba_defend.lua + typescript/bots/FunLib/aba_defend.ts: one new local `bStaleBail = not (jmz.IsSoakCandidate('defstale') and jmz.IsModeTurbo())` in front of the existing condition. Armed, the bail-out does not fire. Nothing else in the file changes.
defstale_20260820.separability: Strictly monotone: armed can only REMOVE this one Action_MoveToLocation-and-return; it cannot add an action, change a bid, or alter any other branch. On a frame where the guard was honestly false the two worlds are byte-for-byte identical (asserted on the control frame). No interaction with roamstale/roamreach/tparrive/tpdead.

odaoe_20260820.fix: New X.od_GetEclipseAoeLocation(hBot, nCastRange, nRadius, nBaseDamage, nMultiplier) + X.od_IsEclipseWorthHitting(hBot, hEnemy, nBaseDamage, nMultiplier). defclose_20260820.defect: aba_defend.GetClosestAllyPos(tPosList, vLocation) -- the arbiter for every 'only the nearest teammate of these roles may defend this building' rule -- scans the role list as if it were 1-based. The TS source walks j = 1..length reading tPosList[j] (0-based array), which tstl renders as tPosList[j+1] in the Lua, i.e. indices 2..#+1. The FIRST role in every list is never compared, index #+1 is nil, and `bestPos or tPosList[1]` falls back to precisely the never-compared role. So {4,5} can only ever answer 5 at ANY distance (or 4, also at any distance, when no role-5 hero is alive); {2,3} can only answer 3, fallback 2; {2,3,4,5} can never answer 2 -- which means ShouldDefend's under-fire gate disqualifies the mid outright, on top of role 1 which is not in the list at all. The distance test the function exists for is inert for the first role of every list; the tie-break degenerates to role number.

retnear_20260820.defect: mode_retreat_generic.GetDesireHelper builds both hero lists at radius 1600 and asks J.WeAreStronger(bot, 1600) beside them, then OVERWRITES the enemy count with a last-seen count taken at radius 3200: `if unseenCount > #nEnemyHeroes then nEnemyNearbyCount = unseenCount end`. Both consumers underneath weigh that 3200-radius number against 1600-radius numbers -- `nEnemyNearbyCount - nAllyNearbyCount > 0` (+0.1875 per surplus) and `not bWeAreStronger and nEnemyNearbyCount >= nAllyNearbyCount` (+0.25). r=3200 is FOUR TIMES the area of r=1600, so the retreat bid leans 'outnumbered' as a matter of geometry: an ally standing 1700 away does not offset an enemy 3100 away, and 3200 is past the bot's own day vision (1800), so every enemy the wide count adds beyond that is one a TEAMMATE sees -- i.e. one that is near the teammate, not near the bot.
retnear_20260820.change: Armed, the count that may replace the nearby count is taken at 1600 (the same radius as the things it is compared with). The WIDE count is still computed and still feeds the 'nothing around at all' discount below (`nEnemyNearbyCount == 0 and unseenCount == 0`), which legitimately wants a wide horizon -- so exactly one lever moves. Armed can only lower or leave the retreat bid, never raise it. bots/mode_retreat_generic.lua only; no TS source for mode_* files.
retnear_20260820.road_not_taken: Widening the ALLY side to 3200 instead. Rejected: nAllyNearbyCount also gates the Oracle / Dazzle / Satanic / Slark discount block, so it moves several levers at once, and there is no last-seen primitive for allies.

The pair says the channel will not survive long enough to pay (the ability deals its damage in pulses over up to 10s, so dying in the first second converts a full ultimate into roughly one pulse). The floor is 0.38 because ConsiderR's own retreat branch already draws the line there ('J.IsRetreating( bot ) and nHP > 0.38'): the file had long agreed CM below 38% is too fragile for the channel and simply never applied that judgement outside the retreat branch -- a source tripwire fails if that branch's literal moves, so the citation cannot go stale. zusult_NOT_PROMOTED_20260820.source: director trigger 2026-08-20T13:00Z; input = replay-check 20260820T110000Z.md section 4 + director's own read of tools/batch_test/behavioral/zusult_gate.py
zusult_NOT_PROMOTED_20260820.decision: zusult NOT promoted. Condition (b) is ruled NOT MEASURED (neither pass nor fail) -- not merely 'unmeasurable'. Stays eligible, may keep riding as a both-arm constant, must not be promoted until the hold-side numbers exist.
zusult_NOT_PROMOTED_20260820.director_independent_check: Read zusult_gate.py source. Its docstring line 1 self-describes as an '(a)-evidence scanner'. Its two aggregated counters are opp (frames where the gate WOULD refuse) and dom (in-domain casts that happened anyway = LEAKS). Both measure gate compliance. Nothing measures what the gate withheld. unaff_frames is computed but printed per-game only and excluded from totals, and is a duration, not a withheld-bid count.
zusult_NOT_PROMOTED_20260820.why_it_matters: GH #59 already established the gate's effective domain is exactly 'the reserve is already spent': it withholds chip casts while R is ready-but-unaffordable, waiting on regen. WITHHOLDING is the gate's primary output, and the observation count on the primary output is zero. #59's own trace (20260820_042607_slot1, 57 consecutive held frames t=463.5-491.5, then Zeus dies at t=492.2 holding 116 mana with R ready and still unaffordable) is the gate working AS DESIGNED, not a defect.
zusult_NOT_PROMOTED_20260820.minimum_b_spec: Per-seed paired, per-game normalized (batch-desk 12:08Z: Zeus candidate-side game count ran +23.8% this wave, so raw counts are guaranteed false positives). (1) in-domain CAST RATE dom/opp armed vs base -- base's dom/opp is the counterfactual base rate and armed's drop below it is the only observable estimate of withheld bids, because a withheld cast emits no event; (2) hold duration: unaff_frames into totals plus the run-length distribution of contiguous gate-true frames; (3) hold PAYOFF: after each hold run, did Zeus actually reach R cost and cast it, and in what fraction did he die first. (3) is zusult's value claim itself and has never been measured.
zusult_NOT_PROMOTED_20260820.cost: no AWS spend needed; computable on the corpus already downloaded

DETECTOR_ASYMMETRY_20260820.rule: section 0b example 17, a new subtype on the MEASUREMENT side (the first sixteen were about an author's reasoning being voided downstream). An execution detector for a SUPPRESSIVE rule (gate/veto/withhold) can only ever see LEAKS, never HOLDS, because a withheld action emits no event. A perfectly obedient and harmful gate therefore scores perfectly on its own detector.
DETECTOR_ASYMMETRY_20260820.corollary_1: the condition (a) detector is NOT the condition (b) detector. (a) asks 'did it run' and a leak rate suffices. (b) asks 'was what it took away worth it' and MUST explicitly measure the withheld side. Writing a (b) conclusion from an (a)-scanner's output is exactly what happened to zusult this round.
DETECTOR_ASYMMETRY_20260820.corollary_2: withheld actions can only be inferred from the control arm: same-domain CAST RATE armed vs base, per-seed paired and per-game normalized -- never a single-arm count. Any suppressive id applying for promote must attach that inferred number.
DETECTOR_ASYMMETRY_20260820.groups_notified: capmono, tpdying, tpdead, defstale, retnear, towerreach are all suppressive; told in test_set.md section R.3 to prepare (b) this way rather than discovering at judgement time that only compliance data exists.

tpdying_DOMAIN_CORRECTION_20260820.correction: tpdying's rationale (and GH #35) reads J.IsInLaningPhase as a clock: 'the frames this floor pins are overwhelmingly POST-laning, where the anticipation is structurally dead'. It is not a clock. In turbo it is `t < 8*60` OR `t < 10*60 and GetBot():GetNetWorth() < 8000`, so between 8:00 and 10:00 the answer depends on the RESPONDER'S OWN WALLET -- and under 8000 at nine minutes is the ordinary case, not the exception.

On that frame it returns... reachable: laning is TRUE at 3068 net worth. So the shipped clause is NOT eliminated. Independently, under the only offline-observable proxy the tpdying predicate reads FALSE on that frame (bristleback 377u + earthshaker 520u dealt 261 into a 504 HP pool) and the pin stays at 0.85 with the id armed. Condition (a) is NOT established; do not spend a wave buying (a) evidence for it on this basis.
tpdying_DOMAIN_CORRECTION_20260820.negative_result: GH #68 section 5.1 (decouple the comparison from current health, e.g. burst >= HP - 0.40*maxHP) is NOT locally validatable. GetEstimatedDamageToTarget is not in a .dem; the loader substitutes realized damage, which ignores the bCurrentlyAvailable flag -- and that flag IS the mechanism GH #68 section 2.3 blames. On the necro frame the strict comparison already passes (1080 vs 965) so a looser one changes nothing; on the tide frame there is no attributable burst at all. Asserted as a [limitation] case. A corpus carrying the engine estimate is the prerequisite for any threshold work on this id.
tpdying_DOMAIN_CORRECTION_20260820.real_defect_underneath: A SURVIVAL release depending on the responder's own net worth is the sharper statement of the same defect: two landers in one fight, same HP, same enemies, get different releases because one is richer. tpdying happens to remove that dependence, so it is correctly designed and wrongly motivated. Not re-gated this round -- the id already exists and its domain is now measured.

liondrainstop_20260820.hero: lion (focus five; SECOND lever for the same shape as liondrain -- one at a time)
liondrainstop_20260820.problem: The shipped X.ConsiderStopDrain is the ONLY way to break a running Mana Drain channel (once it starts, X.SkillsComplement's `if J.CanNotUseAbility(bot) then return` early-out catches IsChanneling and everything else is unreachable). But that release only fires on `J.IsRetreating(bot)` -- and by construction a rooted hero is not walking home, so retreat mode does not kick in during a fight. Result: a channel that STARTS clean and turns unsafe (an enemy walks in / begins hitting Lion mid-channel) rides out its 5s while Lion stands still, taking damage. The FIRST lever `liondrain` only refuses to START unsafe channels; it cannot help a clean start that turned bad.
liondrainstop_20260820.observation: Same 5-game census the first lever built (spot_20260819_180804_1_main). Game 20260819_182855: MODIFIER_ADD t=297.2 -> MODIFIER_REMOVE t=302.2 (5.0s channel, target viper). Lion held position (-5084, 5284) to the tick; 257 hero damage across the 5s + 71 echo slam at t=302.2 caught him standing because he was rooted. Under the pre-liondrainstop shipped code the shipped `if J.IsRetreating` release never fired (he was rooted, not retreating).
liondrainstop_20260820.root_cause: Same shape as cmrguard / cmrself and liondrain: a self-channeled ability with no self-preservation term on the release side. Shipped ConsiderStopDrain reads only J.IsRetreating; the mode is structurally unreachable inside the very state the release needs to break out of.
liondrainstop_20260820.fix: new X.lion_ShouldStopDrain(hBot) in bots/BotLib/hero_lion.lua, consumed in X.ConsiderStopDrain immediately after the shipped J.IsRetreating branch (and INSIDE its own X.IsAbilityEChanneling() clause, so it never fires without a live channel to break). Predicate: SAME as lion_IsDrainSafeToStart with polarity flipped -- hBot:WasRecentlyDamagedByAnyHero(2.0) AND J.GetNearbyHeroes(hBot, X.nEDrainDangerRadius=500, true, BOT_MODE_NONE) non-empty. Reuses the constant X.nEDrainDangerRadius the first lever already asserts in [484, 781), so a retune self-reports on BOTH sides.
liondrainstop_20260820.why_new_id_not_liondrain: Separate levers: start-refusal fires BEFORE the channel begins, stop-release fires AFTER. They live in different Consider* functions and would be untestable jointly (the axeblink trap: two levers bundled where the second's precondition is masked by the first). Independent ids make bisect trivial.
liondrainstop_20260820.why_symmetric_predicate: The signal that decides `do not start` is the same signal that decides `stop what you started` -- if a hero is currently killing Lion inside the danger radius, roots are bad regardless of whether the root is 0.0s or 4.0s old. Deliberate symmetry: any retune of the danger radius must move both levers together, which is what the shared X.nEDrainDangerRadius constant guarantees.

capmono_NOT_PROMOTED_20260820.director_source_finding: THE DETECTOR DOMAIN STRADDLES capmono'S OWN ANALYTIC NO-OP BOUNDARY. Read from source this round (mode_team_roam_generic.lua:102-135, not transcribed): armed = 'raw>0.72 -> 0.72', shipped = 'raw>0.9 -> 0.72'. Therefore capmono's ACTIVE SET is exactly raw in (0.72, 0.9]; for raw>0.9 the two are byte-identical and for raw<=0.72 both are the identity. Intersecting that with the six capped branches' actual bid formulas: (i) laneKill(L287-297) and combo(L302-312) set bLaneKillCommit and are EXEMPTED from the cap at L106 -- capmono can never touch them; (ii) helpCoreTargeted / punish-dive(ownhalf) / overchase all bid 1.96*HP -> capmono is a STRICT NO-OP for HP > 0.9/1.96 = 0.4592; (iii) helpAlly bids 1.633*HP -> raw <= 0.72 hence NO-OP for HP < 0.4408. The replay group's clean domain is HP in [0.42, 0.50], which straddles 0.4592: the dominant 3-branch family is provably inert over ~54% of the sampled HP width. The measured DiD is therefore an ATTENUATED estimate, not a clean null.

DETECTOR_DOMAIN_WIDER_THAN_ACTIVE_SET_20.title: Section 0b, nineteenth example (new subtype): the detector domain is WIDER than the rule's analytic active set
DETECTOR_DOMAIN_WIDER_THAN_ACTIVE_SET_20.pairs_with: the seventeenth example, second subtype (detector predicate STRICTER than the rule -> the rule's real domain is kept out of view). This one is the mirror image: the detector domain is WIDER than the rule's active set, so provably-inert frames are averaged in and the effect is diluted.
DETECTOR_DOMAIN_WIDER_THAN_ACTIVE_SET_20.general_form: For a gate that is a PURE ARITHMETIC TRANSFORM of a desire, its no-op set is solvable in CLOSED FORM from the source (here: raw>0.9 and raw<=0.72, plus every branch structurally exempted upstream). Any detector domain that straddles that boundary yields an ATTENUATED null, and an attenuated null is not evidence of no effect.
corollaries: Every detector domain for an arithmetic gate MUST be intersected with the gate's analytic active set before the number is read.
The complement (the provably-inert sub-domain) MUST be reported alongside as a WITHIN-ARM PLACEBO -- it is free, and it is immune to the cross-seed noise that usually blocks these reads.
Upstream exemptions count: a branch that early-returns before the transform is not in the active set no matter what it bids (here bLaneKillCommit removed l1trade/l5combo entirely).
DETECTOR_DOMAIN_WIDER_THAN_ACTIVE_SET_20.applies_to: every arithmetic-transform id, present and future; capmono is the worked example. Flagged for the retreat/roam desire-shaping family generally.

pre_registered_reading_constraints_H.a_conjunct_vs_disjunct: an unreachable gate is NOT automatically a behavioural defect. AND-conjuncts (unreachable => whole branch dead) and OR-disjuncts (unreachable => harmless redundancy, behaviour unchanged) must be counted SEPARATELY. Director spot-checked the 12 generic ones and BOTH kinds are real: conjuncts at aba_site.lua:760, aba_site.lua:824, ability_item_usage_generic.lua:5749; harmless disjuncts at mode_farm_generic.lua:392 and :506 (J.IsLateGame() sits right next to them).
pre_registered_reading_constraints_H.b_lead_candidate_is_a_CANDIDATE: mode_farm_generic.lua:285 -- 'if bot:GetLevel() >= 18 or not J.IsCore(bot) then return BOT_MODE_DESIRE_NONE end' under 'teamfight location within 2500'. Supports always take the not-IsCore branch; a CORE's only entry is level >= 18 => in Turbo a core structurally never drops farm desire for a nearby teamfight. STOPS THERE: per 0b cases 1-2 (#29/#31), dropping farm desire is NOT going to fight -- it only stops farm from competing. Whether the winning mode changes must be settled by asserting the FINAL desire, never by 'this branch is unreachable'.
pre_registered_reading_constraints_H.c_role_denominator_is_an_UPPER_BOUND: the census does NOT split core/support (#81 just ruled fixture enemy-role reads are constants; own-side roles need --roles). Cores out-level supports, so 'level >= 18 = 0.5%' UNDERSTATES cores. Honest bound: exactly 1 of 210 slots is level >= 18; even if it is NECESSARILY a core and cores are ~40% of slots (~84), cores reaching 18 is bounded by <= 1.2%. Cite this with the words 'upper bound'.

sampling_interval_20260821.finding: FRAME COUNTS IN tools/batch_test/behavioral ARE NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS ROUNDS UNLESS THE DUMP INTERVAL MATCHES, and two documented recipes disagree. dumper/main.go:239 defaults -interval to 1.0s; run_replay.sh:25 -- the path EVERY archived timeline came through -- passes no flag, so archived timelines are 1.0s; but cmrguard_counterfactual.py's usage line said `behav-dump -interval 0.5` and this round followed it.
sampling_interval_20260821.measurement: Same 17-game corpus dumped BOTH ways. Frame counts scale ~2x; EPISODE counts and CAST-side counts do not. esaftershock: domain 4 frames @0.5s vs 2 @1.0s, but 1 EPISODE either way; predicate 15 vs 7 frames, 4 EPISODES either way; withheld casts 1 either way. cmrself (last round's tool, unchanged logic): predicate 61 vs 31 frames -- and the 1.0s column reproduces the 2026-08-21T10:05Z report DIGIT FOR DIGIT (81 -> 31 -> 1, histogram {0:16,1:7,2:8}), so that round's CONCLUSION needs no correction (it quoted episodes: 1 episode / 17 games) but its '31 frames' cannot be compared with odaoe's '30 frames' or axeblink's '21 frames' without first checking each one's interval.
sampling_interval_20260821.why_it_is_a_new_argument: test_set.md section Z.2 already says quote EPISODES, on the grounds that adjacent 0.5s samples inside one standoff are not independent draws. The episode count is the only quantity here that survives a change of sampling rate.

activemode_WORLD_ASSERTION_13_20260821.finding: THIRTEENTH world assertion: bot:GetActiveMode() is bot-VM state, not an entity property, so it is absent from every .dem and therefore from every fixture. The mock falls back to default_for("Get*") = 0 while every BOT_MODE_* name resolves to an auto-id >= 1001, so `GetActiveMode() == BOT_MODE_<anything>` is FALSE on every hero, every frame, all 24 mode names, all 210 shipped comparison lines. Measured over 94 fixtures / 188 team-frames / 872 hero-frames: GetActiveMode()~=0 on 0, and J.IsRetreating / IsGoingOnSomeone / IsDefending / IsPushing / IsLaning / IsDoingRoshan / IsShopping / IsFarming each true on 0/872. J.IsFarming is false for a SECOND independent reason (GetProperTarget nil on 872/872: the corpus carries no neutral units).
activemode_WORLD_ASSERTION_13_20260821.worse_than_its_predecessors: BOTH directions are wrong and they point OPPOSITE ways. Script-side comparison: constant FALSE. Engine-side filter: the loader's GetNearbyHeroes replacement takes the mode argument and discards it (function(self, radius, enemies, _)), so the filter is silently dropped and the call answers "every ally within r" -- measured identical to the unfiltered call on 872/872 frames, which is why J.IsInTeamFight(bot,1500) reads TRUE on 71/872. One missing datum, one family that never fires and one that fires too often.
activemode_WORLD_ASSERTION_13_20260821.consequence_for_gh84: The evidence frame GH #84 section 5 / charter backlog 0i is blocked on (teamfight location non-nil AND inside 2500 AND subject is a core) DOES NOT EXIST and CANNOT BE BOUGHT. J.GetTeamFightLocation ends in GetCenterOfUnits(GetSpecialModeAllies(member,1400,ATTACK)) and GetCenterOfUnits({}) returns Vector(0,0) -- the MAP ORIGIN, not nil. Measured: 6/188 team-frames answer non-nil, 6/6 at the origin, 0 anywhere else; the 7 qualifying hero-frames qualify by standing near the river. All 7 pinned by fixture+hero. The corpus request routed to the replay group is WITHDRAWN: no purchase supplies a datum that is not in a .dem (the dumper field list is pinned to contain nothing mode-shaped), and supplying it would mean MODELLING which mode a bot was in. mode_farm_generic:285 therefore cannot get the (乙) shape under this harness -- its `if` head reads GetTeamFightLocation.
activemode_WORLD_ASSERTION_13_20260821.shipped_reading_not_a_harness_artefact: GetTeamFightLocation uses Vector(0,0) as its empty answer while all 35 consumers test `~= nil`. In game the radii differ -- IsInTeamFight looks 1500 EXCLUDING self, GetSpecialModeAllies looks 1400 INCLUDING self -- so two attack-mode allies in the 1400-1500 shell with the member itself not attacking yields the same empty list and hands "the fight is at the river" to all 35 readers. This harness CANNOT decide how often that band is entered (it would need GetActiveMode). Recorded as a candidate lever with its precondition (in-game observation or a labelled synthetic), NOT proposed as a change. Source shape pinned: no emptiness check between GetCenterOfUnits(allyList) and the return; radii 1500/1400.

gamemode_WORLD_ASSERTION_15_20260821.self_inflicted_leak: M16, found by the FULL suite and not designed: this file leaked its own probe. GAMEMODE_TURBO is a plain global and tests/run_tests.lua is ONE process running every test_*.lua in alphabetical order, so the last honest world() left GAMEMODE_TURBO = 23 installed and every LATER test file ran in the honest world -- silently applying this file's own 21-fixture / 18-winner shift to somebody else's assertions, and turning one of them red. Fixed with unprobe() after every bid and after every probe block, and the state a successor inherits is now itself an assertion ('[premise] the probe does not follow this file into the next one'). TEAM RULE: any test that uses a rawset global as a probe must carry an assertion describing the world it leaves behind -- running the file alone can never surface this, and running the whole suite surfaces it only as an F on an unrelated filename.

zusultx_corpus_preflight_20260821T1930Z.reusable_prior: A new veto being CORRECT is not enough for it to take effect: it also has to be wired into the branch that actually produces the action. (ii) does this frame's action pass through this gate? Question (ii) is a DESK check -- read the consumption points and see which branches hand the gate a nil target. Same family as the wkreincarnmp prior, opposite direction: that one asks whether somebody already vetoes this; this one asks whether the traffic goes past my gate at all.

gamemode15_INDEPENDENT_RECHECK_20260821.the_wrong_inference_and_why_it_looked_ri: At ~19:05Z this session ran `git fetch origin main`; the tip was 936cb3e (replay-check 18:45Z) and NONE of the three artefacts GH #93's body names -- tests/test_gamemode_world_assertion.lua, iterations/reports/strategy/20260821T175822Z.md, the charter entry -- existed in the repository, while the charter's head was still 15:46Z and its backlog still pointed the next trigger at item_purchase_generic:228. This is the mirror image of the 2026-07-23 near-miss ('local green is not remote has'): 'the remote does not have it now' is not 'the remote will never have it'.

cmrcap_20260822.bug: cmrguard's veto ring is `GetCastRange() + X.nRGuardCloseBuffer`. The buffer's justification (GH #34) is CLOSING: a threat only has to cover the gap once during a 10s channel, so give it 400u of walking room. That argument holds for a self-radius CC (cast range 0 -- the holder must physically arrive) and is empty for a ranged one: a Witch Doctor holding paralyzing_cask closes nothing, so on him the buffer is 400 free units of veto radius stacked on a ring that already reaches.

condition_c_reargued.mechanism: A Bone Guard point buys max_skeleton_charges 2/4/6/8 and skeleton damage 34/39/43/49; the COOLDOWN is flat 42s at every rank. X.ConsiderW's only two release branches are thresholds ON THE CAP -- branch 1 `nStack/maxStack >= 0.6`, branch 2 `nStack == maxStack` -- and their only bypass, talent6:IsTrained(), is a level-20 test (GH #84: 0 of 210 turbo hero-slots). So in turbo every Bone Guard point raises, monotonically and on BOTH branches, the absolute bank WK must hold before he releases anything: branch 1 needs 2/3/4/5 charges by rank, branch 2 needs 2/4/6/8. The default row has all four points down by level 7, i.e. from level 7 it asks an 8-charge bank of a hero the batch reads at 15 last hits and 0.6 kills. wkbuild leaves him at cap 2 for the whole laning phase and spends the freed points on the only lockdown he has (2nd Wraithfire Blast point at level 5 instead of 12: stun 1.0->1.2s, cooldown 14->12s) and on maxing Mortal Strike at 8 instead of 10.
condition_c_reargued.strategy_corroboration: Wraithfire Blast is WK's only hard disable and its rank shortens the cooldown 14->12->10->8s; Bone Guard's cooldown is rank-independent (flat 42s). In turbo -- 13-16s respawns, short fight intervals -- cooldown on the only control is the kill-participation lever. Moving points off a non-shortening summon onto the shortening control matches the common public WK skill order (Q/E first, W later).
condition_c_reargued.bounds_self_reported: (1) SIGN, not size: how large a bank WK actually holds between releases is a corpus question and CANNOT be asked offline -- the dumper does not record modifier stack counts (same field family as GH #27 and hero-backlog SS3's magic-wand charges). Nothing here claims a per-game frequency. (2) A higher cap also raises the PAYLOAD per release (8 skeletons at 49 vs 2 at 34); the claim is deliberately one-sided -- the frequency loss is automatic under the shipped rule, the payload gain is conditional on a charge supply nobody has measured. The argument is about the LANING phase, which is exactly the three points wkbuild moves.

itemdesire_WORLD_ASSERTION_16_20260821.finding: SIXTEENTH world assertion: no fixture in this repository has ever called an item's Consider function. J.CanCastAbility(<any item handle>) is FALSE on 5774 occupied item slots / 911 alive hero frames / 98 fixtures. The shipped item loop (ability_item_usage_generic.lua:1007-1035) calls X.ConsiderItemDesire[name](hItem) only inside `if J.CanCastAbility(hItem)`, so the ENTIRE item decision layer is dark: driving the shipped entry point ItemUsageThink() on all 882 drivable hero frames produces ZERO actions and ZERO errors. itemdesire_WORLD_ASSERTION_16_20260821.mechanism: J.CanCastAbility (jmz_func.lua:5145) is a six-clause and-chain: nil / IsNull / IsPassive / IsHidden / not IsTrained / not IsFullyCastable / not IsActivated. The loader (replay_fixture.lua:118-132) wires exactly ONE of the six -- IsFullyCastable -- and for the TP scroll it wires it from the DUMPED cooldown (`IsFullyCastable = u.tp_cd <= 0`). Every other clause falls through to the mock's Is/Has/Can default (false), so IsTrained() answers false and short-circuits the chain TWO CLAUSES BEFORE the one the loader took care over. This is not a missing field: it is a field measured from the replay and then MASKED by two fields nobody thought about, in the same and-chain, in the same helper. 658 of the 911 frames carry a TP scroll whose real cooldown was ready and not one reaches a reader.

unlanded_commit_detector_20260822.what_actually_shipped: tools/agent/unlanded_commits.py + tests/test_unlanded_commits.py (26 checks, 7 mutations all red, rollback green). Recovery repeats; detection does not. Built around two traps this project has paid for: THE SHALLOW CLONE (naive `git log --all --not origin/main` over-reports ~100 commits here; the protection is a REFUSAL, not a filter -- refs with no merge-base are counted and named, 172 of 213 live) and THE REBASE TWIN (patch identity via `git cherry`, not sha identity). Anti-empty-match: always prints refs scanned / commits examined / certifiable / refused; a zero-ref scan exits 2 CANNOT CERTIFY rather than reporting clean; an unreadable trunk exits 2, not a traceback exit 1.
unlanded_commit_detector_20260822.the_tools_own_LIMIT_found_with_real_data: After resetting onto the new main, the tool reports c58de69 and 2ec437a as unlanded WHILE THEIR CONTENT IS ON MAIN as cac2fa5/7de5147. Cause: the relanded copies were MODIFIED (corpus constants 96/863 -> 98/882), so the patch-ids differ and `git cherry` calls them absent. The report is literally true and reads as something stronger than it is. IT DETECTS AN ABSENT PATCH, NOT ABSENT WORK; a finding is a QUESTION, not a verdict, and must be triaged by looking for the content on the trunk first. Written into the tool's own docstring with this measured example -- the limitation is not hidden.
